Hi Sara – thanks for the clear summary and the CSV. Looping in Finance (Rishi, Vanessa) and Billing Ops (Marcus).

Short answer up front: we can support either a single invoice to Blueleaf Singapore or split invoices by Redwood entity — the correct path depends on the "place of supply" evidence you can provide (where the service is consumed) and on whether your EU customers are B2B and have valid EU VAT IDs. Operationally we often prefer a split invoice approach for mixed-consumption customers because it makes reverse-charge and local compliance explicit.

High-level guidance:
- EU consumption (B2B): if the end customer in the EU is B2B and has a valid EU VAT ID, we can issue an invoice from Redwood EU with the VAT line as 0% and the statement "Reverse charge – Article 196 (or local equivalent) applies". We'll run a VIES check and retain the VAT ID evidence.
- APAC / Singapore: services supplied to a Singapore-registered business are generally out-of-scope of EU VAT, but Singapore GST rules may apply depending on place-of-supply and whether the recipient is registered for GST in SG.
- India: import of services can attract tax under reverse charge on the Indian recipient (GST) and there may also be income-tax withholding (TDS) depending on the nature of the service. This is country specific.

Requested next steps from Blueleaf:
1) Confirm which legal entity will accept each invoice (Blueleaf Singapore vs Blueleaf EU entity) and provide registry/VAT IDs (you already started that in the CSV – thank you).
2) Identify which portion of spend is attributable to EU customers (we need customer-level evidence to apply reverse-charge cleanly).
3) Confirm whether Blueleaf prefers us to produce a single consolidated invoice with tax notes or two invoices (Redwood EU + Redwood APAC).

Action from our side: I attached our quick checklist to show required evidence and the standard reverse-charge wording we use. Finance will draft a pro-forma split invoice once you confirm entity routing.

Regards,

Hi all – a few technical points from Tax so the billing decision is informed:

1) EU reverse-charge:
- We require: buyer legal name, VAT ID, country of registration and a business activity statement (customer country of use is helpful).
- Invoice treatment: Redwood EU invoices will show net amounts, VAT = 0, with the annotation "Reverse charge — VAT to be accounted for by the recipient under Article 196 (EU)" and a VIES verification screenshot on file.

2) India (import of services / withholding):
- Two separate mechanisms can occur: GST under reverse charge (recipient accounts for GST in India) and income-tax withholding (TDS) under Indian income-tax rules. TDS is not the same as GST and rates vary by service classification and beneficial ownership.
- Practical ops: if Blueleaf has Indian customers withholding TDS on payments to you, we can either: (a) accept net amounts and provide grossing statements / withholding certificates post-payment, or (b) ask you to remit the withheld taxes and request proof so we can issue gross invoices. We prefer (b) only when the withholding is predictable and supported by documentation.

3) Entity selection:
- To minimize cross-border VAT/GST friction, the cleanest route is a split invoice: Redwood EU (net, reverse-charge) for EU-consumed usage; Redwood APAC or Redwood US for APAC consumption. That reduces the risk of double taxation and simplifies localized remittance.

I will prepare a short pro-forma showing the two-invoice split and include the standard invoice footers and reverse-charge wording for each EU line. If Blueleaf confirms parties and shares the EU VAT cert, we'll run the checks and issue final pro-formas.

- Rishi
